brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A flat pan-fired green tea from the Ending tea farm in Fuzhou, named for the Meizhan and Qilan varieties it is made from.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was developed in 1991 and sold mainly in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Jiangxi and Shanghai. Little more is documented about it.
processing: One bud and one leaf, withered, fixed at high heat and dried slowly at low heat.
appearance_dry: Flat and straight, a glossy green.
appearance_wet: Usually soft green leaf that opens up in the water.
taste_profile: A distinctive varietal aroma with a full, mellow taste that lasts through many infusions.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
